newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended lower on Monday after a sparkling start, but the gains soon diminished and dealers were divided on the reason.
Some dealers said the rising dollar tempered the appetite for European bonds, especially German and Dutch debt, but others said U.S. Treasuries should have jumped at the open on this.
"Treasuries started slipping as well when the U.S. market opened up," said one dealer, adding investors were not switching en masse from European debt into U.S. Treasuries.
"It is probably a number of reasons, among which the current high returns in the share market could be one," said another.
The dealer said the current (moderately low) price levels in the bond market should attact new buyers.
The reaction in the bond market to the firmer dollar was overdone, the dealer said. "If this was the reason," he said, adding he was not all that sure.
The yield spread with Germany widened a touch after the recent narrowing.
But some dealers say the yield gap between guilder-bonds and German bunds in the 10-year segment could become zero, with investors switching out of guilders into marks.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett forecast in its weekly bond market report that Dutch-German 10 year and 30-year spreads would both reach minus five basis points in one month's time.
"The justification for lower Dutch yields remains the healthy state of government finances and the absence of fresh Dutch State Loans supply," it said.
